what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Chad in the Niger: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 1388 Chadian asylum seekers in the Niger, 8.1% of all asylum seekers from Chad.
Refugees from Chad, a separate group, live mostly in the Central African Republic, France, Cameroon and Canada.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Chad in periods from 1997 to 2023, most recently with CCMSR and FACT.
It also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group in Chad in 2015 and from 2017 to 2022.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 12 asylum seekers.
The figure was at its highest, 11902, at the end of 2024, the main year of displacement in the data, and was much lower at the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the Niger.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the Niger only.
